subject: SLO decision roadmap & pilot commitments
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita@mediqhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-07-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: SLO targets and pilot commitments

Hi Anita,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and lots of alignment on where Mediq wants to test Redwood for conversational triage. I wanted to capture the performance targets we discussed (high level) and propose a short mutual action plan so we can lock the pilot dates.

Quick recap of proposed SLOs you asked us to demonstrate during the pilot:
- End-to-end request latency (non-streaming API): p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 550 ms for the canonical 512-token prompts.
- Streaming responses (token-by-token delivery): first-byte latency <= 120 ms for short responses; steady-state per-token latency < 30 ms.
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/s with 250ms median latency under sustained load.
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent chat sessions with KV cache reuse (sessionized requests).
- Stability: error rate < 0.5% (5xx / timeouts) during 4-hour soak and load runs.

Open asks / clarifications from our side:
1) Please confirm whether the p95/p99 targets should include network overhead to your application or if we should optimize to the backend-only numbers (we recommended backend-only above).
2) Share a representative sample trace (anonymized chat transcripts + avg tokens per message) and a small sandbox dataset to run synthetic replay.
3) Confirm the pilot window you prefer (we suggested a 2-week pilot starting the week of July 27).

Proposed MAP (short):
- Week 0: Tech kickoff + data handoff (owners: Ben + Mediq infra)
- Week 1: Canary runs + streaming tuning; gather perf traces (owner: Ben)
- Week 2: Soak + final SLO acceptance (owner: Neha)

I attached a one-page SLO checklist and a draft MAP for clarity. If the high-level targets above look off, please call them out and we’ll revise — want to make sure we’re testing the right tail numbers for your clinical latency needs.

Next steps: if you confirm the sample data and the pilot week above, I’ll loop in Partnerships/legal for the standard pilot MSA and send a calendar invite for a technical kickoff.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta

From: Anita Shah <anita@mediqhealth.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLO targets and pilot commitments

Thanks Rohan — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our engineering and compliance leads: 

- Our acceptance criteria are customer-observed (end-to-end), so please include the network hop to our AWS ALB. As a result, our target for p95 end-to-end can be relaxed to <= 350 ms if your backend-only p95 is <= 300 ms. If backend p95 is 250 ms, that would be ideal.
- For streaming: first-byte is critical for the UI experience. We need first-byte <= 150 ms and per-token <= 40 ms during normal load.
- Concurrency expectation: the 50 concurrent sessions aligns with our peak, but we may spike to 80 briefly — can you confirm graceful degradation behavior if concurrency exceeds the pilot target?

Data & logistics: we will send an anonymized 48-hour transcript sample and a small synthetic traffic generator by EOD Friday. We can do the pilot starting July 27 — prefer July 27 to Aug 9 (2 weeks).

One additional ask from procurement: please include a short note on reserved capacity options and ballpark pilot pricing so our budget team can pre-approve.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Anita
Anita Shah
Director of Platform Engineering | Mediq Health
anita@mediqhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita@mediqhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLO targets and pilot commitments

On Mon, Jul 12, 2026 at 09:05 AM Anita Shah <anita@mediqhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rohan — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our engineering and compliance leads: 
> ...

Great, happy to take point on the technical plan. A few bullets from infra/ops perspective: 
- We will run two phases of synthetic testing: (A) single-host isolation to validate raw backend token latencies, (B) distributed end-to-end with your ALB to capture network overhead.
- Canary ramp: 0 -> 25 -> 50 -> 80 sessions over 2 days, followed by a 4-hour soak at target concurrency.
- Metrics we will collect: p50/p95/p99 latency (req + token stream), redis cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and request error taxonomy. 
- If we observe tail latency increases beyond p99 thresholds during the soak, automatic fallback to a smaller but faster model version will be triggered (we'll document thresholds in the MAP).

Needs from Mediq: a small VPN tunnel or IP allowlist for the pilot agents, sandbox credentials for the ALB endpoint, and the anonymized traces Anita mentioned.

I'll draft a one-page runbook for the canary flow and share it by EOD Tuesday. Also adding a tentative calendar invite for July 27 kickoff — will wait to send until Rohan confirms.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

[Note: internal ops detail — do not share raw GPU telemetry externally; summarize only aggregated metrics in the pilot report.]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita@mediqhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLO targets and pilot commitments — confirmed MAP and next steps

Thanks Anita — good notes and thanks Ben for the ops plan. Finalizing below so we have a single source of truth.

Confirmed SLO framing (we will report both backend-only and end-to-end numbers):
- Backend p95 target: <= 300 ms (aim for 250 ms)
- End-to-end p95 target (including ALB): <= 350 ms
- Streaming first-byte: <= 150 ms; per-token steady-state < 40 ms
- Throughput sustain: 150 req/s; soak profile includes a 4-hour run at target concurrency.
- Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx/timeouts during acceptance window.

Mutual Action Plan (owners & dates):
1) July 15 — Mediq provides anonymized traces + sandbox endpoint + IP allowlist (owner: Anita)
2) July 20 — Redwood provides pilot contract note & reserve capacity estimate (owner: Rohan)
3) July 22 — Ben shares canary runbook and synthetic harness (owner: Ben)
4) July 27 — Tech kickoff + start pilot (owners: Ben / Anita)
5) Aug 7 — Final acceptance run complete; Redwood delivers acceptance report and recommendation (owner: Neha)

Deliverables we will attach to the HubSpot deal: SLO acceptance report, runbook, and a short performance dashboard export. I attached the SLO checklist and MAP again for convenience and included links to the Drive folder and our HubSpot deal.

If that all looks good I will: (a) send a short pilot MSA for signature, (b) share the calendar invite for July 27 tech kickoff, and (c) reserve the pilot capacity on our Dedicated cluster. Anita — can you confirm who on your side will own the IP allowlist + sandbox details?

Best,
Rohan
